questions.q: Which PowerShell module is the current, correct one to install for administering Azure?
questions.explain: Az is the current cross-platform module; AzureRM is the retired predecessor Microsoft deprecated in favor of Az.

questions.q: What is the Azure PowerShell equivalent of `az login`?
questions.explain: Connect-AzAccount opens the same browser-based sign-in flow that az login does on the CLI side.

questions.q: What is the Azure PowerShell equivalent of `az account set --subscription`?
questions.explain: Set-AzContext -Subscription fixes which subscription every subsequent cmdlet in the session targets.

questions.q: Why does seeing New-AzResourceGroup for the first time let you reasonably guess what it does?
options: It follows the Verb-Noun pattern — New creates, and AzResourceGroup is the Azure noun for a resource group
Every Azure cmdlet name is chosen at random with no underlying pattern
AzResourceGroup is a deprecated alias with no predictable meaning
PowerShell cmdlet names only become meaningful after reading the full documentation
questions.explain: New-AzResourceGroup follows the same Verb-Noun pattern taught in the PowerShell Fundamentals course — New creates, and the noun names what it creates.

questions.q: What is the real difference between `az group create --name rg-ps-demo` and `New-AzResourceGroup -Name "rg-ps-demo"`?
options: Different syntax over the same underlying Azure Resource Manager call, with the same result
The PowerShell version creates a resource group in a different Azure region automatically
The CLI version is deprecated and no longer works
They create fundamentally different kinds of resources
questions.explain: Both call the same Azure Resource Manager operation underneath; only the syntax layered on top differs between the CLI and PowerShell.
